question: If an agency is using an approved retroreflectivity-management method but a few individual signs temporarily fall below Table 2A-5, is the agency automatically out of compliance? Include the white-on-red thresholds relevant to STOP-type signs.
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. Per the explanatory (Support) text in Section 2A.22, compliance with the Standard is achieved by having an assessment or management method in place and using it — "an agency or official having jurisdiction would be in compliance with the Standard in Paragraph 2 of this Section even if there are some individual signs that do not meet the minimum retroreflectivity levels at a particular point in time." For white-on-red signs such as STOP signs, Table 2A-5 sets minimum maintained levels of W ≥ 35 and R ≥ 7 (all sheeting types), with a minimum sign contrast ratio of at least 3:1 (white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity). Standards (mandatory): - "Public agencies or officials having jurisdiction shall use an assessment or management method that is designed to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5." (Note: the mandate attaches to using the method, not to every individual sign's condition at every moment.) - "Regulatory, warning, and guide signs (see Section 2A.03), and object markers, shall be retroreflective or illuminated to show the same shape and similar color by both day and night, unless otherwise provided in this Manual for a particular sign or group of signs." - "Regulatory signs shall be retroreflective or illuminated (see Section 2A.21)." — STOP signs are regulatory signs. Guidance (recommended): - One or more of the methods described in "Maintaining Traffic Sign Retroreflectivity" (FHWA-SA-07-020, Revised 2013), or a method developed based on an engineering study, should be used to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5; signs identified through the agency's method as being below the minimum levels should be replaced. Options (permitted): - Highway agencies may exclude certain signs from the retroreflectivity maintenance guidelines: Parking, Standing, and Stopping (R7 and R8 series) signs; Walking/Hitchhiking/Crossing (R9 series, R10-1 through R10-4b) signs; Acknowledgment signs; and Bikeway signs intended for exclusive use by bicyclists or pedestrians. (STOP signs are not among the permitted exclusions.) Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2A-5, "Minimum Maintained Retroreflectivity Levels," including the white-on-red row (W ≥ 35; R ≥ 7) and the minimum contrast-ratio criterion (≥ 3:1) applicable to STOP-type signs. [Image 2] shows the full page containing Section 2A.22, including the Support paragraph stating that an agency using an assessment or management method remains in compliance even if some individual signs are below the minimum levels at a particular point in time. Citations: - Section 2A.22 Standard §2 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Guidance §4 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Option §5 (p.63) - Section 2A.21 Standard §3 (p.62) - Section 2B.01 Standard §3 (p.67) - Table 2A-5 (p.62)
gold_answer: Not automatically. The agency complies by having and using a method designed to maintain the minimums, even if some individual signs fall below them at a particular moment. For white on red, the table gives white at least 35, red at least 7 cd/lx/m², and at least a 3:1 white-to-red contrast ratio.
